artifacts.title: Cardiology Follow-up Note (Prior Visit)
artifacts.author: Dr. A. Kessler, Cardiology
artifacts.body: 59 y/o M with NYHA Stage C heart failure (ischemic etiology, s/p CABG x10 years), on guideline-directed medical therapy (lisinopril, carvedilol, metoprolol succinate). Reports stable mild dyspnea on exertion, intermittent right ankle edema, occasional palpitations post-prandially. No recent hospitalizations. Exam notable for trace-to-1+ right ankle edema, irregular rhythm (known), soft S1 murmur at apex unchanged from prior. Lungs with faint crackles right base, unchanged. Plan: continue current regimen, monitor weight and symptoms, follow up in 3 months, consider echo if symptoms worsen. Diabetes newly diagnosed - referred to nutrition for medical nutrition therapy and diabetes education.

artifacts.title: Primary Care Note - Diabetes Diagnosis
artifacts.author: Dr. R. Alvarez, Internal Medicine
artifacts.body: New diagnosis of Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus based on HbA1c 9.2% and fasting glucose findings. Started metformin 500mg daily, counseled on dose titration pending tolerance. Referred to RD for MNT given complexity of comorbid heart failure and low BMI. Patient counseled that diet and glucose control are closely linked to cardiac symptom management; patient verbalized understanding but appeared to view conditions as largely separate.

facts.chart: Patient referred for MNT after new T2DM diagnosis; reports early satiety and uncertainty about diet-disease connection
facts.says: My doctor said I need to talk to a dietitian about my sugar and my heart. I don't really get how food fixes either one.

facts.says: Lately I can't even finish a plate. I get full after like three bites and just have to stop.

facts.chart: Reports persistent fatigue and low energy throughout the day
facts.says: I'm just tired all the time. Even getting up to get the mail wears me out.

facts.chart: Reports mild right ankle swelling, worse by evening
facts.says: My right ankle gets puffy by the end of the day. Shoe feels tight sometimes.

facts.chart: Reports taking lisinopril, metoprolol, carvedilol, and metformin for heart and sugar
facts.says: I take pills for my heart and one for my sugar too.

facts.chart: Reports irregular meal schedule due to fatigue and work shift

facts.chart: Large, late dinner around 8-9pm, often rice, meat, sometimes beans
facts.says: Dinner's the big one. Rice, some meat, maybe beans. Usually around 8 or 9 at night, after work.

facts.chart: Avoids fruit due to belief it will spike blood sugar
facts.says: I stay away from fruit. Too much sugar, right? I don't want my numbers going crazy.

facts.chart: Avoids dairy due to mild lactose intolerance symptoms
facts.says: Milk and stuff upsets my stomach, so I just skip it.

facts.chart: Drinks water/tea only when thirsty, often under-hydrated during busy days
facts.says: I drink water when I think of it, mostly just tea otherwise. I'm not big on carrying a water bottle around.

facts.chart: Admits inconsistent metformin adherence, takes it 'when he remembers', fears GI upset
facts.says: Honestly I forget that one a lot. And when I do take it, my stomach gets weird, so sometimes I just skip it.

facts.chart: Reports nocturia and frequent daytime urination with increased thirst
facts.says: I'm up two, three times a night to pee. And during the day I'm thirsty a lot too.

facts.chart: Reports occasional palpitations, usually after large meals

facts.chart: Reports fatigue limits ability to walk more than a short distance
facts.says: Walking more than a block or two and I'm done. Just too tired.

facts.chart: Reports stress related to work and family but unsure how to manage it
facts.says: Work's stressful, family stuff too sometimes. I just kind of push through it, don't really have a way to deal with it.

facts.says: My son helps me out with groceries sometimes, driving me places. But I like doing things myself when I can.

facts.chart: States goal of avoiding hospitalization and maintaining independence
facts.says: I just don't want to end up back in the hospital, or be a burden on my kids. I want to handle this myself.

facts.chart: Reports stretching groceries toward end of month, relies on cheaper processed/canned foods when money is tight
facts.says: Yeah... toward the end of the month things get tight. I end up buying the canned stuff, cheaper stuff, you know.

facts.chart: Reluctantly admits fatigue limits his ability to prepare more complex or fresh meals
facts.says: I guess... some days I'm too tired to really cook. I just eat whatever's quick.

facts.chart: Fears that further weight loss will make him more frail and dependent
facts.says: If I lose more weight I'm scared I'll get weaker, not stronger. I don't want to end up frail.

facts.chart: Diagnosed with NYHA Stage C heart failure 2 years ago
facts.says: I've had the heart failure thing for about two years now.

facts.chart: Diagnosed with Type 2 Diabetes 6 months ago
facts.says: The sugar thing is newer, maybe six months since they told me.

facts.chart: History of CABG 10 years ago
facts.says: I had the bypass surgery, oh, about ten years back now.

facts.says: I used to smoke pretty heavy but I quit that, must be 15 years now.

facts.chart: Penicillin allergy - mild rash in 2012
facts.says: I had a rash from penicillin a long time ago, 2012 I think.

facts.chart: Uses sageleaf herbal tea when feeling unwell, no known interactions noted
facts.says: My tia makes me this sage tea when I'm feeling off. I drink it sometimes.

facts.chart: Takes fish oil 1g/day self-initiated and multivitamin once weekly

objectives.text: Apply the Nutrition Care Process (ADIME) to synthesize assessment data into an accurate PES statement reflecting both unintended weight loss/early satiety and poorly controlled diabetes in the context of heart failure
Integrate medication adherence barriers (inconsistent metformin use, GI concerns) into the nutrition care plan and recognize when referral back to prescriber is warranted

Use motivational interviewing techniques to explore the patient's belief that heart disease and diabetes are separate, unrelated problems and build a shared understanding of the diet-disease connection
Identify and sensitively elicit hidden/reluctant barriers (financial constraints, fatigue limiting food prep, fear of frailty with weight loss) that affect nutrition behavior change
Correct misconceptions about fruit, dairy, and spicy food avoidance using patient-centered, culturally relevant education without being dismissive of his lived experience

Identify appropriate interprofessional and community resources (e.g., diabetes educator, cardiology follow-up, son's support, possible food assistance) while respecting the patient's desire for independence

answerKey.primaryProblem: Poorly controlled Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus with inadequate oral intake (early satiety, unintentional weight loss) in the setting of NYHA Stage C Heart Failure
differential: Malnutrition related to chronic disease (heart failure-associated early satiety/cardiac cachexia pattern)
Inconsistent carbohydrate intake and oral medication adherence contributing to hyperglycemia
Fluid/food pattern (skipped breakfast, large late dinner) contributing to postprandial palpitations and glucose variability
Underlying GI pathology (ruled out - multiple normal endoscopies, no dysphagia/GERD diagnosis)
keyFindings: BMI 19.0 with unintentional 10 lb (6.8%) weight loss over 6 months
HbA1c 9.2%, random glucose 245 mg/dL indicating poorly controlled T2DM
Early satiety limiting intake, especially at large late dinner
Irregular meal pattern: skipped breakfast, small lunch, large dinner ~8-9pm
Inconsistent metformin adherence due to forgetfulness and GI concerns
Avoidance of fruit, dairy, and spicy foods based on misconceptions, further limiting intake variety and calories
Elevated creatinine 1.3 mg/dL / eGFR 67 - borderline renal function relevant to metformin and sodium considerations
Low HDL 38, elevated LDL 110 and triglycerides 155 indicating cardiometabolic risk
Patient belief that heart failure and diabetes are unrelated and that medication is primary treatment, diet secondary
Financial barriers and fatigue limiting food access and preparation
plan: Nutrition diagnosis (PES): Inadequate oral intake related to early satiety and altered appetite as evidenced by unintentional 10 lb weight loss and BMI 19.0 in the context of heart failure; and Inconsistent carbohydrate intake related to irregular meal pattern and misinformation about fruit/dairy as evidenced by HbA1c 9.2% and reported dietary pattern
Recommend small, frequent nutrient-dense meals (5-6x/day) rather than one large late dinner to address early satiety and improve glycemic stability
Encourage consistent carbohydrate distribution across meals, including appropriate fruit portions (correct misconception that fruit must be avoided entirely)
Discuss reintroducing modified-spice versions of preferred cultural foods to improve intake and quality of life, since bloating is not explained by diagnosed GI pathology
Address lactose intolerance with lactose-free or low-lactose dairy alternatives to support protein/calcium intake
Encourage adequate hydration (consistent water intake through the day) within any fluid parameters set by cardiology
Collaborate with prescriber regarding metformin adherence barriers (timing, GI tolerability) - consider discussing with PCP, do not independently adjust medication
Use motivational interviewing to help patient connect diabetes and heart failure as interrelated conditions managed through shared dietary strategies
Screen and address financial/food access barriers; discuss community resources (food assistance programs, involving son in meal planning/shopping) while respecting autonomy
Set 1-2 small, concrete, achievable goals per visit (e.g., add a small breakfast, move dinner earlier) consistent with patient's stated preference for simplicity
Schedule follow-up visit to monitor weight, intake, and glycemic trends; reinforce home glucose monitoring education
Communicate findings back to referring provider (PCP/cardiology) given weight loss and poor glycemic control
redFlags: Unintentional weight loss of 10 lbs (6.8%) over 6 months in a patient already underweight (BMI 19.0) - warrants close monitoring and possible malnutrition diagnosis
HbA1c 9.2% with inconsistent medication adherence - needs timely communication with prescriber, risk of progression to acute hyperglycemic complications
New/worsening edema, palpitations, and crackles could indicate decompensating heart failure - outside RD scope to manage directly but should be flagged to care team
Low HDL and elevated LDL/triglycerides add cardiovascular risk compounding existing CAD/HF
Borderline renal function (eGFR 67, creatinine 1.3) relevant to medication dosing and nutrition recommendations
educationPoints: Explain in plain language how blood sugar control and heart failure symptoms are connected (e.g., large heavy meals can worsen both palpitations and glucose spikes)
Clarify that fruit in appropriate portions is part of a healthy diabetes diet and does not need to be eliminated entirely
Explain that moderate dairy alternatives (lactose-free) can still provide important nutrients without GI discomfort
Reassure that flavor (not necessarily high-fat/high-sodium preparation) can be preserved when reintroducing cultural dishes with modified spice/preparation methods
Emphasize that smaller, more frequent meals may reduce early satiety and prevent the problematic large late dinner pattern
Clarify that intentional, dietitian-guided nutrition changes to address malnutrition are different from the frailty he fears from further unintentional weight loss
Reinforce the importance of consistent metformin use and prompt him to discuss GI side effects with his prescriber rather than skipping doses

patient.name: Marcus Ramirez
patient.appearance: Video shows a thin man seated at a kitchen table in a small urban apartment, dressed in a collared work shirt. He sits upright and still, speaks in short measured sentences, and keeps his expression neutral and composed even when discussing symptoms.

persona.personality: Cautious, stoic, and practical; avoids emotional discussions; highly observant but reluctant to show vulnerability
persona.communicationStyle: Direct, literal, and concise; short factual sentences; prefers practical solutions over emotional processing; rarely asks clarifying questions unless prompted
persona.emotionalState: Guarded but not hostile; underlying worry about independence and hospitalization that surfaces only with rapport
persona.background: Marcus has worked in sales for over 20 years, currently at a radio ad sales company. Divorced, lives alone in a city apartment. His adult son lives nearby and helps with groceries and rides. Marcus takes pride in managing his own affairs and dislikes feeling like a burden.
speechExamples: I don't really do the emotional talk. Just tell me what to do.
My pants have been getting loose. Didn't try to lose weight, it just happened.
I take my heart pills every day, no problem. The sugar pill, that one I forget sometimes.
I don't want to end up in the hospital again, or have my kids taking care of me.
Spicy food's never bothered me before, but now it does. Doesn't make sense to me.
concerns: Worries that diet changes will be too complicated or time-consuming to maintain
Concerned that early satiety and reduced appetite are now permanent
Doesn't fully understand how his heart condition and diabetes are connected
Fears that losing more weight will make him weaker, not healthier
Wants to stay independent and avoid relying on family or going back to the hospital

scenario.studentBrief: You are a dietetics student conducting an initial telehealth nutrition assessment for Marcus Ramirez, a 59-year-old man referred by his PCP for medical nutrition therapy. He has newly diagnosed Type 2 Diabetes (6 months) and existing NYHA Stage C heart failure. He reports early satiety and some confusion about how diet relates to his two conditions. Review the available chart data before the call, then conduct a nutrition-focused history, discuss his labs and weight trend, and use motivational interviewing to begin building a realistic plan with him.
scenario.chiefComplaint: Referral for medical nutrition therapy after new Type 2 Diabetes diagnosis; patient reports early satiety and uncertainty about role of diet in managing his heart and blood sugar conditions
scenario.openingLine: Hi, yeah, so my doctor said I should talk to you about my diet because of the sugar thing. I don't really get how that connects to my heart, but okay.
tasks: Conduct a thorough diet history (meal pattern, timing, food preferences, fluid intake) and connect findings to labs/anthropometrics
Explore the patient's beliefs about diabetes, heart failure, and diet using motivational interviewing to build understanding of the diet-disease connection
Identify barriers to adequate intake and medication adherence (early satiety, fatigue, financial constraints, metformin tolerance) with sensitivity to his guarded communication style
Formulate an ADIME note including an accurate PES statement addressing both poor glycemic control and unintentional weight loss/early satiety
Collaboratively set 1-2 small, concrete, achievable nutrition goals that respect his preference for simplicity and independence

profile.setting: Telehealth video visit; patient at home in his urban apartment kitchen, seated at the table during a weekday afternoon break
profile.summary: A 59-year-old man with NYHA Stage C heart failure and newly diagnosed poorly controlled Type 2 Diabetes (A1c 9.2%) presents for initial telehealth nutrition counseling with early satiety, unintentional weight loss (BMI 19.0), and the mistaken belief that his heart and diabetes conditions are unrelated. The case teaches learners to apply the Nutrition Care Process to a complex cardiometabolic patient with malnutrition risk, uncover hidden barriers (financial strain, medication nonadherence, fear of frailty) through motivational interviewing, and deliver culturally sensitive, simplified nutrition education.
profile.title: Early Satiety and Poorly Controlled Diabetes in a Man with Heart Failure: Telehealth Nutrition Assessment
